ai.title: Add ftfilepicker008 and ftfilepickertopk002 to internal view
ai.summary: Added finetunedVertexModels.ft_filepicker_008 and finetunedVertexModels.ft_filepicker_topk_002 to common/src/constants.ts for internal admin file-picker use. Updated backend/src/admin/relabelRuns.ts to target these new models, removing legacy claude/gemini branching logic in favor of unified promptAiSdk calls. Web admin page (web/src/app/admin/file-picker/page.tsx) and tuning script (scripts/ft-file-selection/collect-tuning-data.ts) updated to reflect new model IDs and message history compression.

eli5.text: Internal admin staff who use the file picker tool will now see two updated models available for selecting which AI to run tasks on, replacing older versions. Behind the scenes, the system now sends all messages at once in a simplified format instead of handling different AI providers separately, which makes the process more uniform. If you looked at the tool, you'd notice the model names are updated and the interface still works the same way, just pointing to the newer models.

ai.title: Internal view updated for new ai sdk schema
ai.summary: The `getTracesForUserHandler` in `backend/src/admin/relabelRuns.ts` now uses nullish coalescing to extract `queryBody`. This fallback handles cases where `content[0].text` is missing, accommodating the new AI SDK message schema structure.

eli5.text: When you open a trace of a recent conversation in the internal view, the last message’s text now falls back to the raw content if the structured text field is missing. This means traces using the new AI SDK message schema will still show a readable query instead of falling back to 'Unknown query'. The change is live today and applies to internal staff inspecting these traces; there is no visible effect for outside users.

ai.title: Disable full file context collection
ai.summary: Added `COLLECT_FULL_FILE_CONTEXT` flag set to `false` in `backend/src/main-prompt.ts`. Updated `getFileReadingUpdates` to gate `uploadExpandedFileContextForTraining` behind this flag, stopping the collection of full file context for training data even when files are requested. This prevents sending expanded file contexts to the training pipeline.

eli5.text: The system no longer saves the full contents of code files you open for use in training future models. When you open a file, only the specific parts relevant to your request will be used, rather than the entire file being sent to the training pipeline. A switch that previously collected this full file context has now been turned off, so you won't see expanded file contents being uploaded anymore.

ai.title: Use codebuffConfigFile constant for config path
ai.summary: Replaced hardcoded 'codebuff.json' strings with codebuffConfigFile constant in npm-app/src/dev-process-manager.ts and npm-app/src/menu.ts. Ensures config filename changes propagate automatically to CLI status checks and startup logs. Internal refactor only; no user-facing behavior change.

eli5.text: The setup wizard now displays the configuration file name using the same name the rest of the system uses, instead of showing a hardcoded label. You wouldn't see this unless you ran the setup status check or read the startup logs, where the file name would always match whatever the system is actually looking for. It's a behind-the-scenes consistency fix, so there's no change to how anything works today.

ai.title: Use asSystemMessage for /compact
ai.summary: backend/src/main-prompt.ts wraps the /compact summary content in asSystemMessage instead of passing raw string. Internal refactor. No user-visible change.

eli5.text: When you use the /compact command to summarize your conversation, the assistant now formats that summary as a system message instead of a regular user message. This is a small behind-the-scenes housekeeping change that helps the assistant understand the context better during long conversations. There is no visible difference in how the feature works or looks to you.

ai.title: Add toolFormatter fallback for parsing errors
ai.summary: Added `toolFormatter` invocation in `main-prompt.ts` when `foundParsingError` is true. This triggers a secondary formatting pass on the full response using `relace-api` utilities. Scope limited to backend prompt processing logic. Requires `CoreMessage` and `toolSchema` imports in `relace-api.ts`.

eli5.text: When the assistant's response contains instructions that can't be correctly understood, it now runs a second cleanup pass that tries to repair the formatting using a built-in repair toolkit, then uses that cleaned-up version instead of the broken one. This repair step only runs when such a parsing problem is detected, and the toolkit itself was quietly added to the backend in the same update. The assistant's replies should look more polished and less likely to break when unexpected formatting appears.

ai.title: Enable relace tool formatter in local environment only
ai.summary: The tool formatter execution is now gated by `process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_CB_ENVIRONMENT === 'local'`. This prevents the formatter from running in non-local environments when `foundParsingError` is true. The change applies to `backend/src/main-prompt.ts`.

eli5.text: When the assistant runs into a problem understanding your request, it will now only try a backup cleanup step while you're working on your own computer, not when you're using the hosted version. This keeps the hosted service from doing extra work that could interfere with your session. If you use CodeBuff locally you might see this cleanup happen during failed responses; hosted users won't notice it at all.

ai.title: Relace tool formatter adds message id metadata
ai.summary: The `toolFormatter` function in `backend/src/llm-apis/relace-api.ts` now includes a `relace-metadata` object containing the `codebuff-id` (derived from `messageId`) in the request payload. This change ensures the Relace API receives the specific message ID for better correlation or processing. The modification is internal to the backend API client logic.

eli5.text: When you send a request to the Relace API through the backend, the assistant now includes a small piece of identifying information (a 'codebuff-id') derived from the unique message ID. This is an internal change to the backend logic and doesn't change what you see or experience directly. If you were inspecting the API traffic, you'd notice this additional metadata field in the request payload. The change is live today and helps with tracking and correlating individual requests on the Relace side.

ai.title: ai-sdk prompt functions accept single options object
ai.summary: Refactored `promptAiSdk` and `promptAiSdkStructured` to accept a single object argument instead of separate `messages` and `options` parameters. This change consolidates configuration into one typed object, simplifying call sites across backend utilities like `grade-runs.ts`, `fast-rewrite.ts`, and `gemini-with-fallbacks.ts`. The update aligns internal LLM invocation patterns with the Vercel AI SDK's expected structure, reducing boilerplate in message construction.

eli5.text: The system now bundles all the settings for asking the AI questions into a single package when requesting responses. Developers previously passed questions and settings as separate arguments; they now pass one combined object containing both the messages and the configuration (model choice, session identifiers). If you looked at how these calls are made, you would see the messages nested inside a single options object alongside things like which AI model to use and user-tracking fields. No user-visible behavior changed; this just makes the internal code easier to maintain and keeps the call format aligned with how the underlying AI library expects requests to be structured.

ai.title: Set gemini thinkingBudget to 0 in agent stream
ai.summary: Backend agent stream now sets providerOptions.gemini.thinkingConfig.thinkingBudget to 0 for Gemini models in prompt-agent-stream.ts. This change disables extended thinking for Gemini requests, likely to control token usage or latency. Scope limited to backend streaming logic; no user-facing UI or model picker changes. Note: thinkingBudget is only applied if providerOptions or gemini config are not already set, preserving existing overrides.

eli5.text: The behind-the-scenes assistant that talks to Google's Gemini model has been told to think less before answering. Specifically, it now tells Gemini to use zero extra thinking tokens when generating a response. This is an internal, server-side tweak that mainly makes Gemini's replies come back a bit faster and cost slightly less, without changing how the assistant answers you.

ai.title: Add offline scoring relabel pipeline for filepicker finetunes
ai.summary: feat: add offline scoring. New script `relabel-for-offline-scoring.ts` batches validation traces through `ft_filepicker_005/007/008` and base `gemini-2.0-flash-001`, comparing outputs against `claude-opus-4-20250514-with-full-file-context-new` ground truth. `getTracesAndRelabelsForUser` in `packages/bigquery/src/client.ts` accepts a `cursor` argument for time-based pagination; `collect-tuning-data.ts` exports `isValidationSample` and refactors Gemini history blobbing to tag prior model turns as `<previous_assistant_message>`. `common/src/constants.ts` adds `finetunedVertexModelNames` mapping endpoint IDs to readable names. Covers core constants, BigQuery client, and `scripts/ft-file-selection` tooling.

eli5.text: Developers can now check how well recent AI model upgrades perform by automatically running old prompts through both the old and new versions and comparing the results side by side. This behind-the-scenes tool sorts through thousands of saved conversations, picks out a representative sample, and labels which ones should be used for testing rather than training, so the team can see concrete accuracy improvements before rolling updates out. You won't see this interface directly, but it helps ensure future model updates pick the right files more reliably and accurately over time.

ai.title: PostHog exception autocapture gated to production
ai.summary: Updated `initAnalytics` in `npm-app/src/utils/analytics.ts` to conditionally enable `enableExceptionAutocapture` based on `NEXT_PUBLIC_CB_ENVIRONMENT`. Prevents non-production error noise from reaching PostHog. Scope limited to analytics initialization logic.

eli5.text: If you use the tool in a testing or development setting, error reports from your work no longer get sent to the analytics tracking system called PostHog. Only when the tool is running in the live production environment will it automatically collect and send error information again, reducing clutter from non-live usage. You won't notice anything different unless you check the analytics backend, since this only affects background data collection.

ai.title: Structured error logging across CLI subsystems
ai.summary: Added `logger.error` calls to previously silent or console-only catch blocks in `npm-app`. Replaced bare `console.error` and empty comments with structured logging containing `errorMessage`, `errorStack`, and contextual keys. Covers `chat-storage`, `checkpoints`, `cli-handlers`, `client`, and `create-template-project`.

eli5.text: When the assistant encounters a problem while running in the background, like failing to save a conversation, restore a previous state, or connect to a code repository, it now quietly records a detailed report of what went wrong and where, instead of keeping that information to itself or printing only a brief note to the screen. Previously, many of these failures would either be silently ignored or shown as a simple message, giving no trace of the actual issue. As a result, when something does break behind the scenes, the system's maintainers will have a much clearer record of what happened and in which part of the app, even if you never see the error yourself. This logging is now in place across the app's core functions and is live today.

ai.title: Add structured error logging across npm-app subsystems
ai.summary: Structured `logger.error` calls added to catch blocks and error handlers in `npm-app/src`. Covers `cli.ts` (unhandled rejections, prompt history), `client.ts` (auth, WebSocket actions), `browser-runner.ts` (screenshot, browser close), and `chat-storage.ts` (message persistence). Mechanism: standardizes error reporting by injecting `errorMessage`, `errorStack`, and context-specific fields into logs alongside existing `console.error` output. Scope: internal logging infrastructure for the CLI package; no user-facing behavior changes.

eli5.text: When something goes wrong inside the software, it now writes down more detailed notes about what happened and why, so problems are easier to track down later. These notes are only saved for the team's own troubleshooting; what you see and do day to day stays exactly the same. If you could peek at the logs, you would see clearer, organized messages that include things like which task failed and any relevant error details, making it faster to figure out what needs fixing.

ai.title: maxAgentSteps config limits agent turns
ai.summary: Added maxAgentSteps to CodebuffConfigSchema and codebuff.json. Agent state now tracks agentStepsRemaining, decrementing per turn to enforce the limit. Refactored loadCodebuffConfig to fetch project root internally, simplifying CLI and startup handlers.

eli5.text: If you were having a long back-and-forth with the assistant and it kept going without checking in, it could now run indefinitely. The system has a built-in cap on how many replies the assistant can make in a row before it is required to stop and let you respond, preventing runaway conversations. The default limit is twelve turns, but the project's configuration file has lowered that to five, so the assistant will automatically end its turn after five consecutive replies unless you interject first. You would notice that, instead of the assistant talking forever, it politely stops and asks for your next input after hitting its turn limit.

ai.title: Fix expired message history to include tool results in main prompt
ai.summary: In `backend/src/main-prompt.ts`, `expireMessages` now receives `messagesWithToolResultsAndUser` instead of `messageHistory`. This ensures tool results are correctly expired from the agent state's message history.

eli5.text: When your conversation gets long, the system trims old parts to make room for new messages. This fix makes sure that trimming works correctly when the conversation includes results from tools the assistant used, so nothing important gets accidentally removed from the context that gets sent to the AI model behind the scenes. You may not notice this directly, but it helps keep conversations stable and consistent when tool-based interactions happen.

ai.title: logError no longer throws on uninitialized client
ai.summary: logError now logs an info message and returns early if the analytics client is missing, replacing the previous Error throw. This prevents application crashes during error logging when analytics initialization fails or is skipped. The change is localized to npm-app/src/utils/analytics.ts.

eli5.text: If the analytics service (the thing that tracks app events) isn't turned on or ready when an error occurs, the app now quietly skips saving that error to analytics instead of crashing. You, as a user, wouldn't see anything different during normal use, but crashes caused by failed error-tracking initialization are now prevented. This only affects internal tooling within the package, so regular users are unaffected; the change makes the app slightly more stable when analytics fail to load.

ai.title: Increase codebuff.json maxAgentSteps to 20
ai.summary: Update `maxAgentSteps` in `codebuff.json` from 5 to 20. This change allows the agent to execute more steps per task, potentially handling more complex operations. Scope limited to `codebuff.json` configuration.

eli5.text: The internal assistant tool was given more room to work through complex tasks by allowing four times as many steps per job. This only affects internal tooling used by the development team, not any product or service external users interact with. You wouldn't notice this change unless you are someone configuring or running the assistant, and it is already in effect today.

ai.title: Consecutive assistant steps warning
ai.summary: backend/src/main-prompt.ts injects a system message reporting remaining assistant responses before cutoff. Replaces silent truncation with explicit user-role notification referencing codebuffConfigFile. Internal prompt logic only.

eli5.text: When you're having a long back-and-forth with the assistant and it keeps replying without pause, the system now gives you a clear heads-up instead of silently cutting you off. Before your last few replies, you'll see a message telling you how many responses are left and whether this will be your final one, with a note that you can adjust this limit. If the assistant hits the limit, your turn is ended automatically and a message explaining the cutoff appears. This is live today and affects anyone using the assistant in extended conversations.
